newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended sharply higher on Wednesday, with investors defying a farm crisis and liquidity tightening measures by the central bank to hunt for bargains following recent sharp falls, brokers said.
The benchmark stock index finished 185.90 points or 2.37 percent higher to 8,029.33, more than compensating for Tuesday's 1.3 percent plunge.
Turnover was an active T$115.99 billion, but well below the near-record levels seen during a dramatic rise in recent weeks.
The index, plagued by an outbreak of a deadly hog disease that forced a halt to billions of dollars worth of pork exports, had fallen more than 600 points in the previous four sessions.
"A rebound was to be expected after losing more than 600 points," said analyst Amy Huang of Nomura securities.
Bargain-hunting concentrated on fundamental-backed electronic shares which long have been favourites of foreign institutional investors.
Electronic shares soared by 4.05 percent to lead the overall market recovery.
